summary: Windows-first local document RAG desktop app with WPF/WebView2 shell, in-process .NET backend, React/Vite frontend, SQLite/sqlite-vec storage, Ollama integration, optional LibreOffice conversion, optional PaddleOCR runtime, and Inno Setup packaging.
active_objective: Maintain final handoff readiness for the current Windows setup, verification, build, installer package, and release-evidence workflow.
assumptions: Local development and packaging are Windows/PowerShell-first, while Node and .NET tooling remain standard package managers within that target.
Ignored generated outputs currently present in the checkout are reusable local artifacts, not source state.
decisions: Keep the existing Inno Setup installer technology and add prerequisite checks to existing bootstrap/build/package paths instead of changing installer stack.
Use shared PowerShell prerequisite helpers for .NET SDK and Node/npm so Build-Web, Build-App, and Build-Installer fail before generic native tool errors.
Keep optional Ollama, LibreOffice, OCR Python, and NVIDIA OCR acceleration as manual or user-confirmed feature dependencies rather than blocking app installation.
next_tasks: Run installer lifecycle verification with scripts\Test-InstallerRelease.ps1 -RunInstallLifecycle on a clean Windows verification machine before release.
Provide trusted signing material and Windows SDK signtool.exe, then rerun signed release verification with -RequireSigned before publishing.
Use scripts\Clean.ps1 before a source-only handoff when generated output directories should be removed from the local checkout.
blockers: Signed release verification needs a trusted Windows code-signing certificate, signtool.exe, and a clean Windows verification machine.
risks: Installer OCR preinstall depends on compatible Python 3.10-3.13, pip network access, and PaddlePaddle wheel availability on the target machine.
Local generated outputs are present under ignored paths; use scripts\Clean.ps1 when a clean-output handoff is required.
Installer install/upgrade/uninstall lifecycle was not executed in this pass; package build and non-invasive release evidence passed.
The produced installer is unsigned until trusted signing material and signtool.exe are provided.
PaddleOcrEngine still reads OCR bridge stdout/stderr directly; keep OCR bridge output bounded if future bridge changes can emit large diagnostics.
